findings.title: The Workers’ Compensation Commission (WCC) did not ensure all collections were deposited.
findings.description: WCC lacked an adequate procedure to ensure all collections were deposited as it did not use the initial record of receipts for deposit verification. Collections totaled $26.1 million during fiscal year 2014, but only compared to State accounting records rather than bank deposits.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that WCC perform deposit verifications of collections from the initial record of receipt to deposit in the bank.

findings.title: WCC paid invoices to reimburse the Department of Labor, Licensing, and Regulation (DLLR) for the costs of certain programs without verifying the costs to supporting documentation.
findings.description: WCC paid DLLR invoices totaling $12.2 million in fiscal year 2014 without verifying program costs to supporting documentation. A review disclosed potential overbilling of approximately $471,700 based on budget information, and a similar issue was noted for the fiscal year 2015 invoice.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that WCC a. work with DLLR to establish a process for verifying the invoiced program costs to supporting documentation; and b. determine the propriety of the DLLR invoiced costs for fiscal years 2014 and 2015 and take corrective actions.

extraction.agency_response_summary: WCC acknowledged the control weakness in Finding 1 and agreed to implement reconciliation procedures. For Finding 2, WCC disagreed with the statutory authority required for verification but agreed to continue requesting supporting documentation from DLLR within its limits.
